summary: The Event volume chart on the overview page (24-hour and 7-day views): total events as a neutral grey area, with the high & critical share drawn on top in risk colour. It is built from the charts/core.js helpers (nice axis maximum, linear scales, monotone curves, edge-fading gridlines), redraws through `responsive` when its width changes, plays the clip-path reveal from motion.js on its first draw, and uses the shared tooltip from ui/tooltip.js for its snapping crosshair.

notes.text: Header comment: total volume stays neutral and only the high-risk share gets colour, because in this UI colour always means risk. It also names the two interactions: a clip-path reveal on first draw and a crosshair that snaps to data points on hover.

Imports: `esc` (escapes text before it goes into markup) and `fmt` (number formatting) from dom.js, `animate` and `clipReveal` from the anime.js wrapper motion.js, the shared tooltip, and the drawing helpers from charts/core.js.

JSDoc describing the inputs: the container element, the x-axis `labels`, and a `series` list where each series has a key, a display label, one value per label and a colour (a token like `--critical` or a literal colour), plus an optional height.
Declares `areaChart`, destructuring its options with a default height of 220 px. overview.js calls it from `drawVolume`, once on load and again whenever the 24h/7d toggle changes.
A unique id prefix (like `area-3`) for this chart's gradient, mask and clip-path ids, so they never clash with another chart's.

Swaps each series' colour token for the real colour once, up front, because colours end up in SVG attributes (`stroke`, `stop-color`) where `var()` isn't reliable. The spread `{ ...s }` copies each series instead of mutating the caller's data.

Hands the drawing function to `responsive`, which calls it with the current width `W` and an `animateIn` flag that is true only for the first draw. Returning the result passes the cleanup function back to the page.
Padding inside the SVG reserves room for the axis labels: 36 px on the left for the y-axis numbers and 26 px at the bottom for the x-axis labels.
`H` is the full height; `iw` and `ih` are the inner plotting width and height left after padding.

The y-axis maximum: `flatMap` gathers every value from every series, `Math.max(1, ...)` takes the largest (at least 1, so an empty chart still has a scale), and `niceMax` rounds it up to a round number.
Two linear scales: `x` maps a label index to a pixel across the plot, and `y` maps a value to a pixel with the range written bottom-first, so larger values sit higher (SVG's y axis points down).
Gridline values at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of the nice maximum.

Label thinning: `Math.floor(iw / 64)` estimates how many labels fit at about 64 px each (at least 2), and `every` is the step that stays within that budget. With 24 hourly labels and room for 7, every 4th label is shown.
Builds the markup for each series (`si` is its index); `pts` turns its values into pixel coordinates.
Smooths the points with `monotonePath`, which never overshoots, so the curve never dips below zero or peaks above a real value.
The fill shape reuses the line, then runs straight down to the baseline at the last x, back along the baseline to the first x, and closes with `Z`.

A vertical gradient (from `y1=0` to `y2=1`, top to bottom) running from the series colour to transparent, so the fill fades towards the baseline. The risk series (index 1) starts at 0.32 opacity rather than 0.22 so the risky share reads clearly on top.
The area path filled with that gradient, then the line itself as a stroke with rounded joins, slightly thicker for the risk series (1.8 vs 1.6). The closing `});` ends the map.

Opens the SVG at exactly `W × H` with a matching `viewBox`, so one SVG unit is one screen pixel. `role="img"` and an `aria-label` built from the series names (e.g. All events and High & critical over time) describe the chart to screen readers.
`defs` holds reusable definitions: the edge-fading mask from `fadeMask`, and a clip path containing a full-size rectangle whose width the reveal animates from 0 to `W`.
Dashed horizontal gridlines, one per tick, in 7% white so they barely show, inside a group that uses the fade mask so they dissolve at both ends.
Y-axis labels, right-aligned 8 px left of the plot and nudged down 3.5 px so the 10 px text centres on its gridline; `fmt.num` rounds and adds thousands separators.
X-axis labels: each label is skipped (an empty string) unless its index is a multiple of `every`, but the last label is always kept so the axis ends at the latest period.
The first label is anchored at its start and the last at its end so neither spills past the chart's edges; the rest are centred under their point. `esc` escapes the label text.
The series paths sit inside a group clipped by the clip path; anything outside the clip rectangle is invisible, which is what makes the reveal work.

The hover crosshair, hidden with `opacity="0"`: a vertical line spanning the plot plus one dot per series, filled with the series colour and ringed in the panel background colour (`--s1`) so it stands out from the line.

An invisible rectangle over the plot that catches pointer events; it comes last so it sits on top. `fill="transparent"` still counts as painted for hit-testing, whereas `fill="none"` would let the pointer fall through.
Closes the SVG template, which `innerHTML` turns into real elements.
References to the new elements: the SVG, the crosshair group, its dots (spread into a real array) and the hit rectangle.
`shown` remembers which data index the crosshair is on; -1 means none.

On pointer move, converts the pointer's x into the nearest data index: subtract the SVG's left edge and the padding, divide by the plot width to get 0–1, multiply by the number of gaps, then round and clamp into range. This is the x scale run backwards, and the rounding is what makes the crosshair **snap** to data points.
Only when the index changes: remember it and make the crosshair visible. Skipping DOM writes while the pointer stays near the same point keeps hovering cheap.
Moves the vertical line to the snapped point's x.
Moves each series' dot to that x and to its own value's y; the closing brace ends the `if`.

On every move the tooltip follows the pointer, showing the label as a title and a row per series with its name in the series colour and the formatted value. `esc` guards the text because this is a plain template string, not the escaping `html` tag.
When the pointer leaves, resets `shown` and hides both the crosshair and the tooltip.

First draw only: `clipReveal` grows the clip rectangle's width from 0 to `W` over 1.2 s with a strong ease-in-out (the Bklit-style reveal from motion.js), so the lines and fills wipe in from the left, while the axis labels fade in after 300 ms. On later resizes the chart simply appears.
Closes the drawing callback passed to `responsive`, then `areaChart` itself.
